reasons: Deviation call is correct: the paragraph 2 grant runs only to "Customer", is expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense" and unqualified "revocable", which is at the playbook walk-away line (revocable at Vendor's discretion, no affiliate/contractor path).

Redline reaches the preferred position: it extends the grant to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on its behalf, permits sublicensing to them, makes the licence transferable to successors/assignees permitted under paragraph 8(h), and confines revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4 — removing the at-will revocability.

Edit is proportionate despite the 0.666 changed-character ratio: it preserves "limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive" and the purpose, scope and second sentence, and only rewrites the restrictive string ("non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable") that the rule requires changing; the surviving termination-based revocation in paragraph 4 is expressly preserved rather than deleted.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the three changes, ties transferability to the existing assignment right in 8(h) (a genuine internal inconsistency), and offers the playbook fallback (affiliate coverage on written notice).

Minor, non-blocking: the drafting relies on cross-references to "paragraph 8(h)" and "paragraph 4" while the contract's own revocation text at p0021 cites "section 3"; worth a numbering check on execution, but it does not undermine the edit's validity.
